title: University of Calgary Foothills Faculty of Medicine high-level code and facility review
jurisdiction: Calgary, Alberta (Foothills campus; the report references City of Calgary inspection records but does not establish a reviewing AHJ)
code_edition: Alberta Building Code and Fire Code (edition not stated)

facts.text: GEC Architecture’s report says no prior facility assessments or code/Fire Department/City of Calgary Building Inspection reports were made available; its code review is high-level and recommends a comprehensive detailed analysis for future development.

The report says the University intended occupant load to remain at existing levels but historical records were unavailable; it records an institutional statement that emergency power did not meet facility needs and that fire alarms across four buildings were interconnected, with HRIC and TRW separated by September 2013.

The report lists unclear exit direction and missing evacuation maps in HSC, lack of barrier-free washrooms, possible travel-distance/dead-end-corridor and lobby-exit issues needing review, mechanical breaches of fire separations in HMRB/HSC, emergency-lighting gaps, and washroom capacity/access concerns for large gatherings.
The report recommends comprehensive code analysis, maintaining existing fire separations, evacuation plans/exit mapping and stronger safety quality assurance.

limitations: The readable public copy was downloaded from a third-party Heyzine CDN mirror; the document itself is the GEC Architecture report, but no official University or architect-hosted copy was found in the targeted search.
The report is from 2013 and itself says prior facility and regulatory records were unavailable; its observations must not be presented as current findings.
The report references the City of Calgary, but no reviewing AHJ or permit outcome is established.
